scope_rule: P18–P26 retains its historical county→constituency→ward convergence semantics. The P27–P35 successor programme requires an exact governed 54-indicator framework for every constituency and ward, plus a 47-county audit against the same framework.
denominator_policy: The historical 20115-slot P18–P26 baseline remains auditable and must not be rewritten. P27–P35 creates a successor denominator of 15660 constituency cells and 78300 ward cells, 93960 child-level cells in total, plus a 2538-cell county audit surface.
secondary_source_rules: Secondary evidence is a fallback, not a substitute for an accessible matching primary source.

A primary source that is unavailable, non-responsive, temporarily inaccessible, dynamically rendered or does not publish the required geography/period may trigger secondary-source review after the access/search attempt is recorded.
S2 requires a credible secondary source and an identifiable primary evidence lineage where possible.
S3 requires at least two credible independent evidence lineages that materially agree; repeated copies of one upstream source count once.
Every secondary preferred observation must retain an explicit public label, fallback reason, evidence lineage, verification date and confidence.
Secondary observations must be rechecked for primary-source confirmation or supersession when a suitable primary source becomes available.
conflict_rules: Preserve all defensible competing observations before selecting a preferred value.
Do not average conflicting values merely to create a compromise.
Default selection considers source authority, exact geography match, period/freshness match, methodological fit and independent corroboration.
A newer observation does not automatically outrank an older observation if period or definition differs.
Exact geography outranks an unmatched proxy geography.
Close-scoring, definition-incompatible or materially divergent candidates require manual review.
A published probable-conflicting value must carry conflict=true, confidence, competing-value count and selection rationale.
